financial_summary: Nitori Holdings Co., Ltd. is a large-cap consumer cyclical business with a $13.5B market cap on $5.7B of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at -6% over the past three years, and a shrinking top line is the hardest headwind any business can overcome.
Returns on capital run at 9% against a 7% cost of capital, which means the business barely earns its keep economically. Gross margins of 52% confirm genuine pricing power.

The business throws off $655M in free cash flow — roughly 11 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 1.67× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, the balance sheet carries net cash, which is the gold standard: the business never has to make desperate decisions in a bad year, and interest coverage of 29× is fortress-like.

Shareholder yield is only 0.8%, a thin return of capital, and insider ownership is negligible, so management has little personal stake in the long-term outcome, and within its sector the business captures 1.7× its fair share of profits, a structural advantage visible in the numbers.
